purpose: Treatment-event registry for QUASI_EXPERIMENTS.md design 1 (eligibility-system migration event studies). Dates are recorded at the precision the cited public sources support; nothing here is inferred from memory.

confidence_levels.verified_multi_source: date corroborated by two or more independent public sources
confidence_levels.verified_single_source: date from one credible public source; corroboration pending
confidence_levels.candidate_unverified: event known to exist; dates not yet verified from public records

panel_note: The unblocked outcome panel runs FY2017-FY2024 (analysis/coding_consistency.json). panel_position classifies each event's go-live relative to it; edge events have post-periods in-panel but pre-periods requiring FY2016-or-earlier file acquisition. Source enrichment 2026-08-16 changed metadata only; no state entered or left the registry, so every donor pool is unchanged.

events.system: UHIP (Unified Health Infrastructure Project, later RIBridges)
events.notes: Statewide single-cutover go-live after a one-year delay from the original July 2015 plan; application backlog reached ~15,000 at the crisis peak; FNS billed the state $37,343,809.68 for SNAP overpayments covering September 2016 through December 2019 — a federally documented error-consequence window matching the event.

Integrated SNAP/Medicaid platform (~$101.5M); ~25,000 erroneous cancellation notices and a ~50,000-case backlog after launch; state extended SNAP recertification from six to twelve months as a mitigation — itself an error-process-relevant policy response. no public federal SNAP overpayment billing record located (web search 2026-08-16; absence, not evidence of absence)

Pilot February 6, 2017 (Henry County); Wave 1 May 1, 2017 (46 counties); implemented statewide during 2017; Deloitte Consulting, ~$380M, reported as the largest IT project in state history. no public federal SNAP overpayment billing record located (web search 2026-08-16; absence, not evidence of absence)

events.system: ONE Eligibility (expansion to SNAP and other benefit programs)
events.notes: System runs on code acquired at no cost from Kentucky (Benefind lineage); ~$416M to redesign and maintain; Deloitte holds the support/maintenance contract (~$298M paid, term through 2029) per the October 2024 Oregon Secretary of State audit. The audit found the automated part 'working well' with input errors in 11 of 40 sampled SNAP cases (2024, not launch-era). no public federal SNAP overpayment billing record located (web search 2026-08-16; absence, not evidence of absence). FY2023 QC liability of $15.7M at a 16.7% rate is reported by a secondary source (Mercatus citing FNS) and is the ordinary pre-2025 sanction regime, not a system-specific overpayment claim; unverified against an FNS primary and not used by any estimate.

events.system: NC FAST (Food and Nutrition Services module)
events.notes: County-level FNS rollout ran May 2012 through March 2013; a July 2013 technical failure slowed processing for over a month and drove a benefits backlog. Pre-panel unless the total-rate panel is extended below FY2017.
A ~$205M modernization reported as beginning in 2022 with replacement of the ~30-year-old eligibility mainframe; phase go-live dates not yet verified from primary sources.

Wave rollout: pilot July 22, 2013 (Rio Arriba County); southern counties September 23, 2013; northern counties November 18, 2013; Bernalillo County January 21, 2014. Press documented software glitches snarling food aid. Pre-2017 under the registry's panel taxonomy (which keys to the original FY2017-24 panel) while inside the extended RI/KY FY2012-24 panel; the state was already excluded from every donor pool as a registry entry, so this verification changes no pool. no public federal SNAP overpayment billing record located (web search 2026-08-16; absence, not evidence of absence)

events.system: FSSA eligibility modernization (IBM contract, later canceled)
events.notes: $1.16B ten-year outsourcing contract announced November 2006; regional rollout from 2007; canceled October 2009 by Governor Daniels ('a flawed concept that simply did not work out in practice'); reporting documents >1M denials/losses of food stamps, Medicaid, and cash (+54% denials vs the prior three years) and litigation in both directions. Pre-panel context entry; excluded from donor pools. no public federal SNAP overpayment billing record located (web search 2026-08-16; absence, not evidence of absence)

~$200M system replacing six legacy systems; went live September 1, 2004 despite being unfinished; backlogs left people without food stamps and other benefits; class action by the Colorado Center on Law and Policy won an emergency call center; April 2006 state-auditor report on eligibility determinations. Pre-panel context entry; excluded from donor pools. no public federal SNAP overpayment billing record located (web search 2026-08-16; absence, not evidence of absence)
